title: Moss and the Dragon's Snore
markdown:
Once upon a time, in a valley lit by the moon, lived a young elf named Moss. His cottage roof was soft green moss. Eyes as green as new fern leaves, he watched everything like a deer peeking from the trees. He helped his grandmother Elara, whose fingers were quick as a spider’s. Together they tended glowing mushrooms and collected moon dew that sparkled on the ground. A little curiosity lived in his chest: he often looked toward the woods, wondering about faraway places and creatures he had never seen.

Every day he woke as the sky turned pale pink, helped Elara pour dew into shiny bottles, then went outside to listen. He understood rustling leaves. He could tell time by sunbeams. Sometimes, watching clouds drift, he would wonder: what else is out there?

Until one day, a flutter broke the quiet. A witch floated down, not smoothly, a bit wobbly. Willowisp, known for bright energy and a cloak of sunny colours. Today she looked tired. Pointy hat drooped. Cloak a bit dull. She wrung her hands and sighed like dry leaves on stone. “Oh, dear me. I need to choose a pet. So many choices. It’s too much.”

Moss stepped forward, voice soft as a breeze. “Can I help, Mistress Willowisp? Our woods have many small charming creatures.”

Big eyes blinked. A spark of hope. “Would you? I need a friend who understands my special kind of magic. Finding the right one feels like catching a rainbow.”

It was not a journey of fighting. A gentle exploration. Cool air, damp earth, sweet pine. They tiptoed past shy glow-worms, lights blinking like fallen stars. “Too quiet,” Willowisp said. “I need a friend with a little more spirit.”

A happy stream whispered over smooth stones. Water sprites, laughter like tinkling bells. “Lovely. But they might splash my spell ingredients into a soggy mess. And my drying rack is very important.”

A rocky path, wind singing. Plump marmots whistled hello, noses twitching. “Busy little fellows. Perhaps they like their naps too much to keep up with my energetic brewing.”

Shoulders drooped. “It seems no one is quite right. Maybe I’m meant to be alone, with only my cooking pots.” The leaves rustled as if they agreed too readily.

Moss remembered his mossy cottage, Elara’s calm, the sure presence of home. “Patience now. There’s a place not far, where moonlight gathers like pools of water. Very peaceful.”

Through hanging vines, a hidden grove: velvety moss, silver ferns like little rolled papers, moonlight falling like liquid silver. In the middle of moss so soft it looked made of moonlight, a baby dragon no bigger than a round pinecone, fast asleep. A gentle snore rumbled, warming the air. Toasted marshmallows. Moss, without quite deciding to, thought of the dragon as Rumble.

Willowisp knelt. The dragon stirred, unfurled a tiny wing, sleepy chirp. Warmth from the small body. Pine needles and marshmallow. She did not name the feeling. She only whispered, “He is perfect. He fits.” Tiny tears of happiness. The air shimmered gold.

Ever since that afternoon, Willowisp and Moss have met for moonlit teas in the peaceful valley, sharing quiet stories. Rumble snores under the silver ferns, and the cooking pots, for once, have company. The most wonderful friends arrive not through big adventures, but through a grove that smells of marshmallow, and a snore that sounds like staying.
